recentItems.title: Is Trump testing the limits of US power? | The Bottom Line
recentItems.description:
Host Steve Clemons asks The Hill’s Niall Stanage and Politico’s Irie Sentner about the fortunes of both major United States parties – Republican and Democrat – in the upcoming November 3 local elections.

Stanage argues that the Trump administration’s conversion of the US-Iran war into an economic war is meant to take the issue out of the limelight, at least until the election is over.

But the war, and the rising prices it has caused, are weighing heavily on the minds of voters, argues Sentner.

recentItems.title: Israel and Greece sign $3.4bn defence deal in Tel Aviv after three years of talks
recentItems.description:
Greece is strengthening its air defences as the war in Ukraine changes the rules of engagement across Europe. 

The country is buying three Israeli systems: Spyder, Barak and David’s Sling, designed to intercept drones, aircraft and cruise missiles. 

Al Jazeera’s John Psaropoulos reports from Athens.

recentItems.title: More value in Cairo’s trash, but less for those who collect it | AJ #shorts
recentItems.description:
The Zabaleen area, where the waste from Egypt’s capital is sorted, is seeing demand for its recycled materials surge as the war on Iran disrupts imports. But rising costs and new competitors mean the traditional recyclers aren’t necessarily better off.

recentItems.title: Europe turns to carbon capture: Denmark’s Greensand project aims to cut the cost
recentItems.description:
Wildfires sweeping across Europe this summer have intensified calls for urgent action to meet climate targets. The EU is placing some of its hopes on carbon capture and storage technology, which traps CO₂ and injects it deep underground. The technology is costly, but a new project in Denmark hopes to change that.

Al Jazeera’s Paul Rhys reports from the North Sea.

recentItems.title: Somalia hunger crisis: Nearly 2 million children are expected to go Hungry
recentItems.description:
The UN says nearly two million children in Somalia could face hunger this year. Hospital admissions for malnutrition have risen 32 per cent; those admissions often involve serious health complications. International aid cuts have also forced several health and nutrition centres to close.

Al Jazeera’s Haru Mutasa reports.

recentItems.title: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation leaders meet in Kyrgyzstan for security and trade talks
recentItems.description:
Shanghai Cooperation Organisation leaders are gathering for talks in Kyrgyzstan. It's a security and economic bloc with ten member states. The summit is focused on security, trade and regional cooperation, while major powers are also set to hold key bilateral meetings. 

Al Jazeera’s Osama Bin Javaid reports from Bishkek.

recentItems.title: Nepal army enters hydro tunnels searching for trapped workers | AJ #shorts
recentItems.description:
Nepal’s army is searching hydro tunnels filled with mud and debris for more than 900 workers believed to still be trapped after last week’s devastating floods. Over 4,200 people are missing, as the death toll continues to climb.
